title: Japanese Sums Delta I
author: sfushidahardy
rules:
Japanese Sums Delta I

This ruleset is inspired by Jesper's incredible Castle Wall Delta. A much more challenging puzzle is coming soon. I'd love to set and solve more variants of puzzles with some notion of "delta-ification" in future. I hope you enjoy it!

Rules:

• Shade some cells in the grid and place a digit from 1 through 6 in every unshaded cell. Digits may not repeat in rows or columns. Additionally, draw a directed "ice-like" loop which consists of vertical and horizontal line segments between centers of cells, and does not branch but may cross itself. The loop must not cross itself on unshaded cells and must not turn on shaded cells. The loop visits every cell of the grid.

• Japanese Sums Delta: outside clues indicate the signed sums of groups of digits in their respective row or column, in order, where shaded cells serve as delimiters between groups. A "?" may be any integer. In a given row or column, either all clues or no clues are given.

• By a signed sum, we mean: the value of a digit contributes positively if there is a directed loop segment passing into or out of its cell while moving towards the outside clue. The value of a digit contributes negatively if there is a loop segment passing into or out of its cell while moving away from the clue. The value of a digit is 0 otherwise.
